adult-teeth.why: Check it yourself with your tongue; 32 permanent and 20 baby teeth, wisdom teeth at 17 to 25, confirmed. An easy opener.

blinks-per-minute.why: Check it yourself: a blink every few seconds; 'around 17 blinks per minute in a laboratory setting' and 4 or 5 when reading confirmed.

billion-dollars-a-second.why: Fermi: a year is about 31.5 million seconds; the page's gigasecond ('over 31 years and 287 days', within 1% of 31.69) and megasecond (11 d 13 h) confirm the answer and the fact.

world-cup-2026-matches.why: Fermi from the definition: 12 groups of 6 matches, then a 32-team knockout; 104 matches, up from 64, confirmed now the tournament is over.

monopoly-board-spaces.why: Check it yourself: four corners and nine squares a side; 'forty spaces containing twenty-eight properties' confirmed. An easy opener.

football-panels.why: Check it yourself: picture each black patch ringed by white ones; twelve pentagons and twenty hexagons, the Telstar pattern, confirmed.

smartphones-shipped.why: Fermi: a few billion owners replacing a phone every two or three years; 1.54 billion in 2019 and the first billion (55% of phones) in 2013 confirmed.

cars-in-the-world.why: Fermi from cars per person, rich countries against the rest; 1.644 billion in January 2025 and the trillion litres of fuel confirmed.

big-mac-calories.why: Reason from yourself: a burger is a big part of one meal of a 2,000-a-day diet; 580 kcal in the US and 306 of them from fat confirmed. An easy opener.

italian-pasta-per-year.why: Fermi from your own plate, about 100 g on most days; 23.5 kg a person in 2015, ahead of Tunisia's 16, confirmed (the page's 2008 'over 27' is within 1.5x).

vatican-population.why: Fermi from its size, a few city blocks round a basilica: hundreds, not thousands; 882 residents in 2024 confirmed, and who they are explains the number.

last-woolly-mammoths.why: Ice Age animals, so a guess of 10,000 years is within 3x; the last ones on Wrangel Island until 4,000 years ago (the mainland's 10,000) confirmed: a real surprise.

north-pole-to-equator.why: Fermi: a quarter of Earth's 40,000 km; the metre as a ten-millionth of it ('setting 10000 km') confirmed, and why it's so round is the reveal.

russia-time-zones.why: Fact was beside the point (its fourteen neighbours); now the page's 9,000 km and 172 degrees of longitude (19 E to 169 W), which explain the 11. Eleven confirmed.

countries-in-africa.why: Go round the map, or a quarter of the world's countries; 54 fully recognised states confirmed, and keeping the colonial borders explains why so many.

birthday-pairs.why: Reason from yourself: most school classes of 25 to 30 had two with the same birthday; 23 and its 253 pairs confirmed, the classic surprise against the 183 of first instinct.

coca-cola-can-sugar.why: Reason from sugar cubes of about 4 g, ten or so a can; 39 g in a 355 ml can with no fat and 140 calories confirmed (38 g in another line, within 3%).

ball-in-play-minutes.why: Reason from watching: throw-ins, free kicks and injuries; 'a 90-minute game typically involves about an hour of effective playing time' confirmed.

new-zealand-sheep.why: Fermi from its 5 million people and the famous sheep; 23.3 million in June 2024 and the 39 million (about 10 a person) of 2007 confirmed, forestry named as the cause.

formula-one-race-distance.why: Monaco's 260 km in the fact isn't on the source; now the page's own point, laps set to make up the distance. Fermi from 1.5 hours at about 200 km/h; 305 km confirmed.

a4-sheets-per-square-metre.why: Check it yourself: 21 by 30 cm, about 16 to a square metre; A0 defined as 1 m2 and A4 a sixteenth of it confirmed: arithmetic with a reveal.

us-mcdonalds.why: Fermi from a McDonald's for every town of 20,000 to 30,000; 13,697 in the list's table (December 2025), China's 7,700 and Japan's 3,025 confirmed.

english-speakers.why: Fermi from the native-speaking countries plus India, Nigeria and learners; Ethnologue 2026's 1,493 million and the 450 million native confirmed; the page's 'as many as two billion' is 1.34x, inside 1.5x.

london-underground-underground.why: Picture the map: deep tunnels in the middle, long open branches; 'only 45% of the network is underground' confirmed, and the Tube being mostly above ground is the surprise.

pacific-ocean-share.why: Fermi: water covers about 70% and the Pacific is nearly half of it; 32% of the surface, larger than all the land combined, confirmed.

brazil-coffee-share.why: The biggest grower among dozens of tropical countries: big, not a majority; 31% in 2023 and about 70% of exports in the 1910s confirmed.

canada-maple-syrup-share.why: Was quebec-maple-syrup-share: Quebec's 72% is undated, and the page's 2025 figures (Canada over 75%, 90% of it Quebec's) put it near 68, over 3 points off; now Canada's dated share, 75% in 2025 with the US about 25%, Quebec in the fact.

penalties-scored-share.why: Reason from watching: most go in, but you've seen saves; 74.25% in the Bundesliga 1963-2004 confirmed (recent leagues 76.5 to 79.8), and World Cup shootouts' 69.4% teaches.

drive-on-the-left-share.why: Fermi: India alone is a sixth of the world, then Indonesia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Japan, the UK; 'about a third of its population' and a sixth of the land confirmed.

reykjavik-share.why: A population share carries its year: '2026' added from the page (1 January 2026); 64%, the city's 140,000 and the six municipalities around it confirmed.

swiss-alps-share.why: Picture the map: mountains across the middle and the south; 'about 60% of the country's area' confirmed, and most people on the plateau is the twist.

canada-near-border-share.why: Picture the map: Toronto, Montreal, Vancouver and Ottawa all near the border; 'about 80 percent ... within 150 kilometres' confirmed.

iceberg-underwater-share.why: Check it yourself with an ice cube in a glass; about a tenth above water, from 920 against 1,025 kg a cubic metre, confirmed. An easy opener.

pluto-demoted.why: Your own life: eight planets at school or nine; the IAU's August 2006 definition, after Eris, confirmed. An easy opener.

euro-cash-arrives.why: Your own life or your parents': just after 2000; coins and notes on 1 January 2002, after the 1999 accounting euro, confirmed.

first-traffic-lights.why: Horse-drawn traffic means before cars: Victorian London; December 1868 on Parliament Square and the constable's semaphore arms and lamps confirmed.

first-world-cup.why: Between the wars, decades before any World Cup you remember; 1930 in Uruguay, for the centenary of its independence, confirmed.

world-population-4-billion.why: Fermi: 8 billion in 2022 and a doubling in about 50 years; 1974 (the milestone table, and April 1974 by the Census Bureau) and the 48 years to 8 billion confirmed.

first-balloon-flight.why: Before railways and planes, in the France of the Montgolfiers; Étienne's tethered ascent from the Réveillon yard in October 1783 confirmed.

elizabeth-ii-becomes-queen.why: Arithmetic from the 70-year reign that ended in 2022; queen from 6 February 1952, aged 25, confirmed (the 1953 coronation is a year off and still scores 98). An easy opener.

web-goes-public.why: Dated two ways on its page: the lead's 'opened to the public in 1993' against the release 'to the whole Internet on 23 August 1991'; now asks for that release, and the fact no longer repeats it.

last-moonwalk.why: From the first landing in 1969 and a handful of missions after; Apollo 17 in December 1972, and nobody past low orbit until April 2026, confirmed. An easy opener.

first-selfie.why: 'Selfie' read two ways (a phone picture, or any photo of yourself), a gotcha that sent phone-age guesses to 0; the definition now says any camera, so photography's start is the way in. 1839 and Cornelius's note confirmed.
